thread:
sanjay: Ran perfetto + nvprof on the xfer/batching change (PR #4823). Short summary: overall tail p99 latency up ~12% and GPU busy time increased. nvprof top kernels pasted below.
maya: can you drop the raw table? curious if this is a hot kernel shift or just launch overhead.
sanjay: paste below (nvprof simplified):
```
nvprof summary (GPU time incl): total 14.234s
1) cudnnConvolutionForward        6.041s   42.3%   SM Util 78%
2) cutlass_gemm_kernel            3.088s   21.7%   SM Util 92%
3) aten_layer_norm_cuda           1.296s    9.1%   SM Util 34%
4) kv_cache_read_kernel           1.082s    7.6%   SM Util 12%   (lots of tiny launches - avg 120us)
5) attention_softmax_kernel         0.783s   5.5%   SM Util 66%
6) dropout_mask_pack               0.411s   2.9%   SM Util 15%
others (trivial kernels / memcpy)   1.533s  10.9%
```
sanjay: perfetto timeline shows a long tail of small KV read kernels interleaved between big GEMM launches — looks like the new batching heuristic increased KV scatter/reads frequency for long-seq requests. The large cudnn/gemm kernels still dominate, but the KV kernel count increased ~3x which seems to raise launch overhead and reduce effective concurrency.
chloe: is SM util for kv_cache_read_kernel actually that low? 12% seems like launch/IO bound. Could be many tiny grid launches (1 block) + memcpy syncs.
sanjay: yup - sample perfetto slices: many yellow micro-slices ~80-200us each. Also observed a CPU <-> GPU cudaMemcpySync for small payloads between them.
maya: hypothesis: batching heuristic changed to 'eager kv read per sample' rather than grouped read per microbatch. So number of device launches scaled with sequence length. That would explain p99 regressions on long sequences.
tj: quick microbench plan: 1) reproduce with nvprof on synthetic workload of batch=1..8 long-seq; 2) run with CUDA Graph capture (persistent kernel) enabled; 3) try grouping KV reads on host and issuing single batched kernel. I'll instrument with CUPTI counters and produce a small flame graph.
perf-bot: run triggered: perf/job/4823-smoketest started by @sanjay (ETA 18m)
sanjay: immediate mitigations we can try: 1) fall back to grouped-kv-read in routing policy for long-seq requests; 2) increase batching window (might impact latency); 3) fuse tiny kernels (kv read + pack) on CPU side before kernel launch; 4) experiment with CUDA Graphs/persistent threads to amortize launch cost.
chloe: agree. Also need to check occupancy on cutlass_gemm_kernel — it's high SM util but may be starving due to repeated fragmentation from small kv kernels. If we can coalesce kv ops into fewer launches, cudnn/cutlass can run at steadier occupancy.
maya: have we regressed throughput for short-seq workloads? or only long-seq p99? My quick dashboards: short-seq throughput unchanged, long-seq p95->p99 widened.
sanjay: exactly. commit 4f3b9ad changed commit batching heuristic, likely intended to reduce memory pressure but inadvertently increased per-request small-kernel churn.
tj: I'll run the microbench and post nvprof + perfetto traces into this thread. Will also add a small table: kernel, calls, total_time_ms, avg_ms, SM_util as CSV so we can rank programmatically.
maya: thanks. once tj posts, let's decide whether to revert heuristic or ship a targeted fix (grouped-kv-read) behind a flag. @sanjay please open an issue linking traces and perf bot job.
sanjay: on it. filing ISSUE-2167 with attached traces and patch suggestion. cc @chloe

chloe: FYI, if we go the CUDA Graph route, micro-ops need to be deterministic; batching heuristic variability will make capture harder. Probably grouped-kv-read is the least invasive short-term fix. :+1:
sanjay: ok plan: tj run microbench + upload artifacts, i'll open revert PR/feature flag branch pending results. If tj confirms launch overhead is dominant we'll prioritize grouped-kv-read.
tj: noted. starting now, will update in ~25m.
